model: TLB4 four-channel weight transmitter (Modbus RTU / Modbus TCP)
applies_to: Laumas TLB4 with the Modbus RTU port or the Modbus/TCP option; communication protocols manual version 1.12. Direct registers only.
summary: The TLB4 is a DIN-rail weight transmitter for up to four load cells. Over Modbus RTU (or the Modbus/TCP version, which uses the same register list) it exposes gross, net and peak weight, a status word, digital I/O, setpoints and calibration values as holding registers, and takes commands (tare, zero, save) through a single command register. This map lists the directly addressed registers; settings reached through the exchange registers are left out.

addressing.note: Registers are printed 40001-40074. Laumas says to subtract 40001 for a 0-based client (40028 -> 27). The manual's read example asks for start address 0x0007 to read gross weight at 40008, confirming the offset.

source.title: TLB4 User Manual - Communication Protocols
source.pages: pp. 2-14 (fieldbus parameters, SR1, command status, Modbus RTU register list, examples), p. 38 (Modbus/TCP), pp. 46-79 (command procedures)

notes: Host: this copy is hosted by AutomationDirect, not by Laumas; a short search did not find the same protocols manual as a direct download on laumas.com.

Word order: every 32-bit value is an H/L register pair with the high word at the lower address. The manual's read example returns gross weight 4000 as 0x0000 0x0FA0 at 40008-40009, so ABCD is documented.

Weights (GW, NW, PW) are positive magnitudes with the decimals implied by the division setting (DU low byte); the sign comes from SR1 bits 7-9. The manual says the calibration weight CALW is a signed 32-bit number (two's complement for negatives). It does not state signedness for setpoints, hysteresis, analog weights or preset tare; they are typed INT32 here, which only matters for negative values.

Left out: exchange registers 40051-40064 (R1/W1, EXC, AEXC). The list prints them as fourteen single registers while the other fieldbuses describe R1/W1 and EXC/AEXC as 4-byte values, and the exact register split for Modbus is not stated.
Parameters such as filter, sensitivity, full scale and zero tracking are reached by writing W1 and sending a 65xx command to CMDR; they are not listed because they go through the exchange registers.
Program type matters: peak weight, display coefficient, setpoints and CMDOUT are BASE program features; instrument status IS is LOAD program only.
Serial settings (baud, parity, address 1-99) are set from the instrument's own menu; the protocols manual does not give factory values.

integration.summary: Read 40007-40013 in one FC3 request: status word, then gross, net and peak weight as 32-bit H/L pairs. Apply the sign bits from the status word and the decimals from the division index. Write 7 / 9 / 8 to the command register 40006 for tare on, tare off and zero.

minimum_registers.why: Status: stability, sign and load-cell errors
Division index for the implied decimals

integration.enable: Select Modbus RTU in the instrument's serial communication menu and set address, baud, parity and stop bits there. The Modbus/TCP version gets its IP address from the Lantronix DeviceInstaller tool and listens on port 502.
quirks: Only FC3 and FC16 are supported; use FC16 even for a single register (the manual's examples write with FC16).
Weights carry no sign: check SR1 bits 7 (gross), 8 (net), 9 (peak).
Setpoints and some values are written to EEPROM (limited to about 100000 writes); setpoints themselves stay in RAM until command 99.
setup: Set the RS-485 address (1-99), baud rate, parity and stop bits in the instrument's serial communication setting menu.
For Modbus/TCP use port 502; the register set is identical to RTU.
gotchas: Broadcast (address 0) writes are executed with no reply; broadcast reads are ignored.
Setpoints and hysteresis values are set to zero if the calibration is changed significantly.

registers.name: Program type
registers.description: BASE or LOAD program; some registers apply to one program only.

registers.name: Command register (CMDR)
registers.description: Write a command code to run it; see notes for the codes.

values.101: Acquire single calibration point (sample weight in CALW)
values.106: Acquire one of multiple calibration points

registers.name: Status register (SR1)
registers.description: Weight sign, stability and error flags.

bits.3: Gross weight over 110% of full scale

registers.name: Gross weight (GW)
registers.description: Magnitude without decimal point; sign is SR1 bit 7.

registers.name: Net weight (NW)
registers.description: Magnitude without decimal point; sign is SR1 bit 8.

registers.name: Peak weight (PW)
registers.description: Magnitude without decimal point; sign is SR1 bit 9. BASE program.

registers.name: Divisions and units of measure (DU)
registers.description: High byte = unit index, low byte = division index (decimals).

registers.name: Setpoint 1 (SP1)
registers.description: Weight value without decimal point. RAM only until command 99.

registers.name: Setpoint 2 (SP2)
registers.description: Weight value without decimal point. RAM only until command 99.

registers.name: Setpoint 3 (SP3)
registers.description: Weight value without decimal point. RAM only until command 99.

registers.name: Instrument status (IS)
registers.description: LOAD program only: batching state code.

registers.name: Sample weight for calibration (CALW)
registers.description: Write the loaded test weight, then command 101 or 106; reads back 0 when OK.

registers.name: Analog output zero weight (ANA0)
registers.description: Weight giving analog zero; saved to EEPROM.

registers.name: Analog output full-scale weight (ANAFS)
registers.description: Weight giving analog full scale; saved to EEPROM.

registers.name: Preset tare (PT)
registers.description: Write the tare, then command 130 to apply it.
